questions.stem: Which nerves does a rectus sheath block target?
options: Ends of the 6th, 7th and 8th intercostal nerves
Ends of the 1st and 2nd lumbar nerves
Ends of the 12th thoracic and ilioinguinal nerves
Ends of the 9th, 10th and 11th intercostal nerves

questions.stem: How do the ends of the rectus sheath nerves reach the skin?
questions.answer: As anterior cutaneous branches to the periumbilical skin

questions.stem: After which operation is a rectus sheath block used for analgesia?
options: Umbilical hernia repair and other umbilical surgery

questions.stem: What is an indication for a rectus sheath block at a laparoscopic port?
options: Iliac fossa port of laparoscopic surgery

questions.stem: In the landmark rectus sheath block, where is the local anaesthetic injected?
options: Into the rectus muscle belly itself
On the posterior sheath, through the anterior sheath and rectus muscle
Into the subcutaneous fat above the sheath

questions.stem: Where is the entry point for a landmark rectus sheath block?
options: At the midline, 5 cm below the umbilicus
Over the iliac crest, 10 cm lateral to the midline
Directly over the umbilicus, in the midline
2–3 cm from the midline, just above the umbilicus, at the top of the rectus bulge

questions.stem: What needle is used for a landmark rectus sheath block?
options: Short-bevel 5 cm needle at right angles to the skin
Winged infusion needle inserted parallel to skin

questions.stem: Why is the depth to the posterior rectus sheath hard to predict?
questions.answer: It correlates poorly with age, weight or height

questions.stem: A landmark rectus sheath block injects ____ in 5 ml aliquots.
In what aliquot size is the landmark rectus sheath injectate given?
Where is the ultrasound probe placed for a rectus sheath block?
questions.answer: Transverse, just lateral to the umbilicus or at the linea semilunaris

questions.stem: What is the target spread for an ultrasound-guided rectus sheath block?
questions.answer: Between the rectus muscle and posterior rectus sheath

questions.stem: Which needle approaches are described for ultrasound-guided rectus sheath block?
options: Only in-plane, at a shallow angle
Neither; it is a landmark block only

questions.stem: What volume per side is used for an ultrasound rectus sheath block in adults?
What volume per side is used for an ultrasound rectus sheath block in children?
Which structure lies just deep to the posterior rectus sheath, a risk when injecting?
In up to what proportion of patients is a rectus sheath block incomplete from anatomy?
Why can a rectus sheath block be incomplete despite good spread?
questions.answer: Anterior cutaneous branches form before the sheath and never pierce its posterior wall
